text.meta_title: ZeRechnung · Factur-X, ZUGFeRD and XRechnung e-invoices in Go
text.meta_description: Open-source Go package to create, read and validate e-invoices: Factur-X, ZUGFeRD, XRechnung, Peppol, UBL, FatturaPA and Facturae. Pure Go, standard library only.
text.review_notice: This translation has not been reviewed by a native speaker yet.
text.hero_title: E-invoices in Go, from the PDFs you already make
text.hero_lead: Keep generating your invoice PDFs the way you do today. ZeRechnung adds the XML invoice and the metadata the standard requires, and the PDF becomes a compliant Factur-X or ZUGFeRD e-invoice. It also reads and validates the invoices you receive.
text.hero_status: Version 0: the API may still change before v1.
text.gopher_alt: The Go gopher, in glasses and a paper boat hat, reads an invoice ledger at a desk with a typewriter, between stacks of invoices.
text.features_lead: One package for the whole life of an e-invoice, on the sending side and on the receiving side.
text.f_create_text: Turn the PDF your application renders into a Factur-X or ZUGFeRD invoice. Totals and the VAT breakdown are worked out with exact decimals, and an invalid invoice is refused before anything is written.
text.f_read_text: Read hybrid PDFs and plain XML, in CII or UBL, from every ZUGFeRD version since 1.0. Data the model has no field for is kept, and written back in place.
text.f_validate_text: Check the schemas, the EN 16931 rules, the profile rules and the national rules of France, Germany, the Netherlands and Italy, as well as Peppol. Each finding gives the official rule ID and the XPath of the element.
text.f_convert_text: Convert between CII, UBL, FatturaPA and Facturae, and rewrite a PDF as PDF/A-3 when that needs no PDF engine. When it does, you get the reasons, page by page.
text.w_pure_text: No CGO, no Java, no external binary, no network call. `go get` is all the setup there is.
text.w_accurate_text: Every pull request compares the results with KoSIT, Mustang and veraPDF, invoice by invoice. A new difference fails the build.
text.w_fast_text: Reading and fully validating a typical invoice takes about 25 µs, five times less than with the next fastest Go package.
text.w_intact_title: Your PDF stays as it is
text.w_intact_text: The XML is added with an incremental update. The original bytes are untouched, so an existing signature remains valid.
text.formats_lead: One invoice model, `invoice.Invoice`, for every syntax: converting from one to another is a parse and a marshal.
text.fmt_facturx_note: profiles MINIMUM to EXTENDED, and EXTENDED-CTC-FR
text.fmt_xsd: XSD schema, XAdES signature; EN 16931 through UBL or CII
text.accuracy_lead: Every pull request runs the reference validators on the official test corpora and compares their results with those of ZeRechnung, invoice by invoice.
text.acc_kosit: XRechnung invoices with exactly the same errors as the KoSIT validator.
text.acc_mustang: invoices with the same errors as Mustang. Each difference comes from the references themselves and is explained.
text.acc_npa: NLCIUS files with the same rules as the Dutch NPa validators. The other differences are justified.
text.acc_verapdf: invalid PDF/A files of the veraPDF corpus caught by a rule of the right clause.
text.accuracy_link: Method and limitations, on the wiki
text.start_install: Install the package. It needs Go 1.24 or later.
text.start_create: Turn your PDF into a Factur-X invoice.
text.start_validate: Validate an invoice you received, with the national rules of the seller's country.
text.start_cli: Or use the command line. `validate` exits with code 1 on errors, so it fits in a CI pipeline as is.
text.open_title: Open source, and open to contributions
text.open_text: ZeRechnung is free software under the MIT license. Bug reports, differences with a reference validator and missing rules are welcome.
text.translate_text: Translations are open to everyone. Spotted a mistake in your language?

text.examples_lead: Each example is a complete Go program that runs as it is. It creates a real e-invoice, checks it against the rules of the country, then reads it back. The tests of the repository run every program and check that it prints what this page shows.

text.benchmarks_meta_description: Execution times and allocated memory of ZeRechnung compared with 14 other Go libraries and 85 libraries in eight other languages, on the official ZUGFeRD corpus, with CPU use and peak memory.
text.benchmarks_lead: ZeRechnung was measured against 14 other Go libraries, then against 85 TypeScript, Python, Rust, Java, C#, C, C++ and PHP libraries: same files from the official ZUGFeRD corpus, same machine, same harness. Every result is checked before it is timed, then what one call allocates is counted.
text.bm_gain: {1} faster than the next Go library
text.bm_when: Measured on {1} on an Apple M4 Pro, on one goroutine, with ZeRechnung {2}.
text.bm_go_lead: The other libraries read XML with `encoding/xml`, whose tokenizer alone takes 96 µs on a 13 KB invoice. ZeRechnung has its own XML reader and goes well below that floor. A lazy PDF reader, which reads only the objects it needs, and an incremental update to add the invoice do the rest.
text.bm_scale: The bars are on a logarithmic scale: each grid line is ten times slower than the one before. Times are medians of three runs.
text.bm_poly_lead: For each operation, the fastest Factur-X library of each language among those that succeed. ZeRechnung leads in reading a 13 KB invoice, writing it, embedding it in a PDF and validating it with all the EN 16931 rules; Kura (C++) extracts the XML 8% faster. On the 1.3 MB XML and on checking a PDF, libraries that do less come first: see the notes under their names. The details of each library are in the repository.
text.bm_poly_when: Measured on {1} on the same machine, on one thread, with ZeRechnung at commit {2}.

text.bm_op_inject: Embed the XML in a PDF

text.bm_in_host_stream: host PDF with xref streams, 136 KB
text.bm_flagged_note: Last column: how many of the 26 valid invoices of the corpus the library reports as invalid. The official schematrons report 6, so 6 is the right answer.

text.bm_res_title: CPU and peak memory, by language
text.bm_res_lead: Each library ran alone in its own process, one per operation: loading, check, first call, then a timed series of one second. Peak memory: the maximum resident memory of the process, runtime included. CPU / wall time: the processor time of all the threads of the process over the elapsed time; 100% = one busy core.
text.bm_res_go: ZeRechnung fits in 17 to 26 MiB depending on the operation. Above 100%, the Go garbage collector is working in parallel on other cores: confined to one core (`GOMAXPROCS=1`), ZeRechnung uses 5 to 47% less CPU, for a wall time 4 to 38% longer.
text.bm_res_others: Rust, C and C++ stay under 10 MiB at the median. The JVM sizes its heap from the memory of the machine, hence the Java figures; Node and .NET start at 65 and 70 MiB. The two PHP libraries that hand the extraction to the pdfdetach program are left out: that child process escapes the measurement.
text.bm_note_bytesearch: searches the bytes for the XML, misses 72 PDFs out of 104
text.bm_correct_text: Speed means nothing if the verdicts are wrong. On the 26 valid invoices of the official corpus, the official schematrons report 6: rule BR-CL-25 twice, and CII-SR-465 on the four XRECHNUNG examples. ZeRechnung reports exactly these 6, and extracts the XML of all 104 PDF files of the corpus. Its CI also compares every pull request with the KoSIT and Mustang validators.
text.bm_correct_poly: Among the 85 libraries in other languages, 17 give the verdicts of the reference, nearly all by running the official schematrons: 0.4 to 72 ms per invoice. The most downloaded ones stop at the XSD schema or at recomputing the totals, or only generate invoices.
text.bm_method_text: One module per library, called through its public API in the most direct way its documentation offers. Every timing starts with a correctness check: the extracted XML must be a CII invoice, and a PDF produced by an injection must be read back. The harnesses are in the repository, so anyone can run them again.
text.bm_env_median: median of 3 runs, on one thread, with the bytes already in memory
text.bm_mem_title: Memory, compared with the other Go libraries
text.bm_mem_lead: What one call allocates: the bytes and the number of allocations, as `go test -benchmem` counts them. It is all the memory the call asks for, including what it frees before it returns, and so the work it leaves to the garbage collector. ZeRechnung allocates the least on every operation.
text.bm_mem_scale: The bars are on a logarithmic scale: each grid line stands for ten times more memory than the one before. Under each value, the number of allocations.
text.bm_mem_floor: Dashed line: {1}, what `encoding/xml` allocates just to split the file into tokens.
text.bm_mem_poly_lead: For each operation, the library of each language that allocates the least among those that succeed. ZeRechnung allocates the least to read, validate, write and embed. Rust and Python count every allocation; V8 does not count its own, so TypeScript shows only the bytes, measured from the growth of its heap. Java, C#, C, C++ and PHP have no counter yet.
text.bm_env_alloc: bytes and allocations of one call: go test -benchmem; a counting allocator in Rust; every malloc in Python (PYTHONMALLOC=malloc); heap growth in Node
text.compliance_meta_description: E-invoicing obligations in every European country, simplified, and the checkpoints ZeRechnung lets you follow: EN 16931, Factur-X, XRechnung, Peppol, FatturaPA.
text.compliance_lead: Which standard does each European country require, and since when? Which of its checkpoints can ZeRechnung verify before an invoice leaves? A simplified overview first, then the detail for the countries with rules of their own.
text.cp_frame_text: Since 2019, the directive 2014/55/EU requires every public buyer in the EU to accept invoices that follow the European standard EN 16931, in the UBL or CII syntax. Each country adds its own rules, formats and dates for invoices between companies. With the ViDA package, e-invoices become the rule for trade within the EU on 1 July 2030.
text.cp_scope_text: ZeRechnung creates, reads and validates invoices. Sending them, through an approved platform, a Peppol access point or the Italian SDI, and reporting to the tax administration are the job of those platforms: no library does it for you.
text.cp_overview_lead: B2G: invoices to public buyers. B2B: invoices between companies. The last column gives the main formats of the country, and whether ZeRechnung checks them.
text.cp_legend_partial: the EN 16931 rules apply, not the national ones
text.cp_legend_no: a national format, outside UBL and CII
text.cp_asof: Status on {1}. Dates change often: check the official source of a country before relying on one.
text.cp_link_norms: Standards by country, with their sources (wiki, in French)
text.cp_details_lead: For the countries whose rules ZeRechnung implements, or where it is often used: what the country requires, and what the package checks. The names in code are the rule sets of `validate.Options`.
text.cp_guide: Guide for this country, on the wiki
text.cp_rules_lead: The EN 16931 rules always apply. National rules are added by rule set, or from the country of the seller with `Auto`. Every finding gives the official identifier of the rule and the XPath of the element.
text.cp_rules_auto: adds the rules of the seller's country
text.cp_fr_intro: Chorus Pro for public buyers since 2017. Since 1 September 2026, every company must be able to receive e-invoices through an approved platform. Large and mid-sized companies send them already, small ones from 1 September 2027.

text.cp_fr_brfr: French rules BR-FR (FNFE-MPE 1.4.0.04): SIREN and SIRET, electronic addresses, mandatory notes, billing frame
text.cp_fr_syntax: UBL and CII invoices at the EN 16931 and EXTENDED-CTC-FR profiles, which approved platforms must accept
text.cp_fr_chorus: Chorus Pro: SIRET of the public buyer, service code and commitment number when it requires them
text.cp_fr_pdf: PDF/A-3 container: attached XML, XMP metadata, AFRelationship
text.cp_fr_sign: PAdES signature of Factur-X invoices, one of the three means of authenticity and integrity (CGI art. 289 VII), and check of received signatures
text.cp_fr_send: Sending through an approved platform, and e-reporting to the tax administration
text.cp_de_intro: XRechnung for public buyers since 2020. Every company must be able to receive e-invoices since 2025. Sending them becomes mandatory in 2027 above €800,000 of turnover, and for all companies in 2028. XRechnung and ZUGFeRD from version 2.0.1 are accepted.
text.cp_de_xrechnung: XRechnung 3.0.2 in CII and UBL, with the rules and severities of KoSIT
text.cp_de_ids: Leitweg-ID and GEBA identifiers of public buyers, with their check digits
text.cp_de_profiles: ZUGFeRD profiles accepted by the BMF for B2B: neither MINIMUM nor BASIC WL
text.cp_de_zf1: ZUGFeRD 1.0 invoices received: read, with minimal checks, since the format predates EN 16931
text.cp_de_send: Sending to the federal portal OZG-RE or over Peppol
text.cp_it_intro: Since 2019, every invoice, to public buyers, companies and consumers alike, goes through the Sistema di Interscambio (SDI) in the FatturaPA format. Public buyers also accept EN 16931 invoices that follow the Italian CIUS.
text.cp_it_fatturapa: FatturaPA 1.2 (FPA12 and FPR12): read, write, XSD schema 1.2.4
text.cp_it_cius: CIUS-IT rules of the Regole tecniche 2.7 (appendix 2), in UBL and CII
text.cp_it_ext: EXT-IT extensions of domestic invoices (rules BR-IT-DE)
text.cp_it_split: Split payment (scissione dei pagamenti, VAT category B) in the totals
text.cp_it_sdi: Checks only the SDI can do: existence of VAT numbers, duplicates
text.cp_it_sign: CAdES and XAdES signature of FatturaPA files, and check of received signatures
text.cp_it_send: Sending to the SDI and handling its receipts
text.cp_nl_intro: Public buyers require NLCIUS or Peppol BIS invoices since 2017. Mandatory e-invoices between companies are announced for 1 July 2030.
text.cp_be_intro: Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 is mandatory between companies since 1 January 2026. Near real-time e-reporting is planned for 2028.
text.cp_be_peppol: Peppol BIS Billing 3.0, mandatory in B2B, in UBL and CII
text.cp_be_kbo: Belgian enterprise number (scheme 0208), with its check digits
text.cp_es_intro: Facturae on FACe for public buyers since 2015. E-invoices between companies become mandatory on 6 October 2027 above €8 million of turnover, a year later for the others, in UBL, CII, EDIFACT or Facturae.
text.cp_es_en16931: EN 16931 invoices in UBL or CII, two of the four syntaxes allowed in B2B
text.cp_es_peppol: Peppol BIS Billing 3.0, accepted on private platforms
text.cp_es_facturae: Facturae 3.2, 3.2.1 and 3.2.2, the format of FACe: read, write, XSD schema
text.cp_es_sign: XAdES-EPES signature of Facturae invoices under the signature policy of Facturae v3.1, and check of received signatures: policy, role of the signer, certificate
text.cp_es_verifactu: VERI*FACTU invoicing software and SII reporting
text.cp_pt_intro: Large companies invoice public buyers in CIUS-PT since 2021. There is no structured B2B obligation, but invoices are reported to the tax authority every month and carry an ATCUD code and a QR code.
text.cp_pt_cius: CIUS-PT 2.1.1 (UBL) for public buyers: the rules of the schematron of eSPap, BR-CIUS-PT and DT-CIUS-PT, and its versions of the EN 16931 rules
text.cp_pt_nif: Check digit of the Portuguese VAT number (NIF), as a warning
text.cp_pt_atcud: ATCUD code and QR code on every invoice
text.cp_pt_saft: SAF-T (PT) and monthly reporting of invoices
text.cp_pt_sign: Qualified electronic signature or seal of PDF invoices (PAdES, with your qualified certificate)
text.cp_ro_intro: Every invoice issued in Romania goes through RO e-Factura, the platform of ANAF: to public buyers since 2022, between companies since 2024 and to consumers since 2025. The invoices follow the CIUS-RO, in UBL or CII.
text.cp_ro_cius: CIUS-RO 1.0.1 for every invoice: the rules of the schematron 1.0.9 of ANAF, BR-RO and BR-DEC-RO, in UBL, and their transposition to CII
text.cp_ro_cif: Check digit of the Romanian tax identification code (CUI/CIF), as a warning
text.cp_ro_send: Upload to RO e-Factura (SPV of ANAF), the signature of the ministry and the conversion to PDF
text.cp_sk_intro: From 1 January 2027, invoices between VAT payers established in Slovakia, to companies and to public buyers, are electronic: Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 in UBL, sent over Peppol, with their data reported to the Finančná správa. Cross-border invoices follow on 1 July 2030.
text.cp_sk_peppol: Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 in UBL, with the type 384 between two Slovak parties
text.cp_sk_rules: What the transposition 1.13 of the Finančná správa requires beyond Peppol BIS: postal addresses, VAT identifier (IČ DPH), IČO, legal form and register entry of the seller, VAT point date, reference of a corrective invoice
text.cp_sk_ids: Electronic addresses of scheme 0245 (DIČ) of the Slovak parties, and the format of the DIČ, IČ DPH and IČO
text.cp_sk_tdd: Tax data document (TDD SK) reported to the Finančná správa by the access points
text.cp_ie_intro: Public buyers accept EN 16931 and Peppol invoices since 2019. Revenue plans e-invoices between companies, with real-time reporting, from 1 November 2028, starting with large companies.
text.cp_ie_b2g: Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 and EN 16931 for public buyers
text.cp_ie_b2b: B2B e-invoices from 2028: EN 16931 and Peppol apply, the Irish specifications are not published yet
